details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 3.3, paragraph beginning "With Semble: in addition to the targeted block, run a Semble query for each conflicted symbol's name (extracted from the hunk via simple regex — existing code in review_conflict_prepare.sh already does this for the 'affected symbols' log line)." | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan claims existing code in `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` already extracts conflicted symbol names for the "affected symbols" log line, but that code does not exist.
  WHY: Reviewers only found an unrelated "Only tracked files are affected;" cleanup comment, so the instruction points implementers at nonexistent infrastructure.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 6.1, first bullet | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan says "The `setup uv` step (already present in some — audit during rollout)" even though uv is described elsewhere as a new dependency and no setup-uv usage exists in the repo.
  WHY: The contradiction can make implementers assume `setup uv` is already present and skip adding it where it is needed.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 4.1 diagram; Section 4.2 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan describes `uv tool install semble` caching around a `uv.lock` file, but `uv tool install` does not use a lockfile and the later cache-key description is different.
  WHY: The document gives inconsistent caching guidance and refers implementers to a nonexistent `uv.lock`-based mechanism.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 5.1 Phase 1 checklist | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The Phase 1 checklist only adds `SEMBLE_FALLBACK`, but Section 8.1 says both `SEMBLE_FALLBACK` and `SEMBLE_QUERY` are contractual log prefixes.
  WHY: Following the checklist literally would omit `SEMBLE_QUERY`, breaking the observability and cost-audit contract the plan depends on.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 5.1, first bullet | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan tells implementers to add a "Build semble index" step to `.github/workflows/ai-implement.yml`, but that is not the internal workflow file.
  WHY: Implementers will look at or edit the wrong workflow path instead of the actual internal workflow.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 5.5 and 6.1 template file listings | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The plan lists `ai-review.yml` as a template to update, but the review autofix workflow template is named `review_autofix.yml`.
  WHY: This points rollout work at the wrong template name and risks leaving the real review-autofix path without the Semble changes.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 4.5 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan cites `scripts/write_codex_config.sh` lines 14-22 for the v0.113+ apply_patch rationale, but that line range does not match the cited text.
  WHY: Readers checking the citation will land on different content and may doubt the document’s accuracy.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Sections 6.3, 6.4, 7.3, 7.4 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The plan cites CLAUDE.md for unattended-pipeline rules, but the unattended pipeline is supposed to use `unattended_system_instructions.md` instead.
  WHY: Referencing the wrong authority document can send implementers to the wrong rule source for backward compatibility, MongoDB, and GH_PAT policy.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 2.3 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: Acceptance criterion 2 requires cross-repo token-cost telemetry evidence, but the plan never says who collects it, when it is collected, or whether it gates merge.
  WHY: The criterion is underspecified and can remain perpetually pending without an owner or timeline.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 8.2 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The plan says to extend `scripts/cost_audit.py` for Semble byte buckets but does not specify a parser for the `SEMBLE_QUERY ... bytes=...` log lines.
  WHY: Without a concrete parse pattern, the new Semble-byte metric can silently stay at zero.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 4.4 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `semble_query_block` pseudocode does not include the timeout wrapper that the risk table claims exists.
  WHY: An implementer following the pseudocode verbatim would omit the timeout guard and leave queries able to hang until the job timeout kills the runner.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 3.7 and Section 5.4 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Section 3.7 treats `scripts/render_prompt.sh` as "stays grep-only," while Section 5.4 requires adding `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}` handling to that same script.
  WHY: A reader can conclude the script is off-limits and miss the placeholder work needed for Semble prefetch content.
- docs/semble-integration-plan.md:Section 4.4 query envelope comment | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The proposed 5-second timeout may be too tight for the first query on a large corpus or a cold runner.
  WHY: It can create avoidable fallback noise and mask genuine indexing problems on slower consumer repos.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
